prompt: Density $f(X) = (\lambda/2)e^{-\lambda|X-a|}$, $\lambda > 0$. Observations: $-7,-5,-3,1,2,6,10$. (1) For fixed $\lambda$, find the MLE of $a$. (2) Find the MLE of $\lambda$ at that $a$. (3) In a new world with $a = 2$ known but only censored data (of 20 obs, 5 are $> 15$ and 15 are $\le 15$), find the MLE of $\lambda$.
solution: (1) $\partial_a\ell = \lambda\sum_i[\mathbb{1}(a<x_i) - \mathbb{1}(a>x_i)]$; setting to zero, $\hat a$ = sample median $= 1$. (2) $\partial_\lambda\ell = n/\lambda - \sum_i|x_i - 1| = 0$ gives $\hat\lambda = n/\sum_i|x_i-1| = 7/33$. (3) $P(X>15) = \frac12 e^{-13\lambda}$ (with $a=2$). The likelihood is $\binom{20}{5}(\frac12 e^{-13\lambda})^5(1 - \frac12 e^{-13\lambda})^{15}$; maximizing gives $\frac12 e^{-13\lambda} = 1/4$, i.e. $e^{-13\lambda} = 1/2$, so $\hat\lambda = -\frac1{13}\log(0.5) \approx 0.0533$.

prompt: Cholesterol measured before and after 6 months of a new drug on 10 patients (paired data). (1) Determine whether the drug reduced cholesterol from baseline (state $H_0, H_1$; assume normality). (2) Give a 95% CI for the final cholesterol of an 11th randomly recruited patient. (3) What design mistake was made?
solution: (1) Paired $t$-test: $H_0:$ mean reduction $= 0$ vs $H_1:$ mean (Final $-$ Baseline) $< 0$. Mean change $= -14$, $s = 18.38$, SE $= 5.81$, $T = -14/5.81 = -2.4 < -1.833 = t_{9,0.05}$ — reject $H_0$ (drug reduces cholesterol). (2) Using final values: mean $206$, $s = 14.30$; 95% prediction interval $206 \pm t_{9,0.975}\,s\sqrt{1 + 1/10} = 206 \pm 2.262(14.30)(1.049) \approx (172.1, 239.9)$. (3) No untreated control group — cannot separate the drug effect from time/placebo effects.

prompt: Generate $X$ from $f(x) = 2x$ ($0<x<1$) if $Y=1$, or $g(x) = 3x^2$ if $Y=0$, where $P(Y=1) = 1/2$. (1) Find the cdf of $X$. (2) Find $P(Y=1 \mid X \le 1/2)$. (3) Find $\operatorname{Cov}(X, Y)$.
solution: (1) $F(x) = x^2$ under $f$, $G(x) = x^3$ under $g$, so the marginal cdf is $(x^2 + x^3)/2$, $0<x<1$. (2) $P(Y=1\mid X\le\tfrac12) = \frac{(1/2)^2\cdot(1/2)}{[(1/2)^2 + (1/2)^3]/2} = 2/3$. (3) $\mathbb{E}[X\mid Y=1] = 2/3$, $\mathbb{E}[X\mid Y=0] = 3/4$, so $\mathbb{E} X = 17/24$, $\mathbb{E} Y = 1/2$, $\mathbb{E}[XY] = \frac12\cdot\frac23 = 1/3$; $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y) = 1/3 - (17/24)(1/2) = 1/48$.

prompt: $X$ has density $f(x\mid\theta) = 2x/\theta^2$, $0 < x < \theta$. (1) Find $\mathbb{E}_\theta X$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\theta X$. (2) Under squared-error loss, among estimators $\delta_c(x) = cx$, find the $c$ minimizing MSE. (3) Is that estimator unbiased for $\theta$? (4) Find an unbiased estimator of $\theta(1-\theta)$.
solution: (1) $\mathbb{E}_\theta X = 2\theta/3$, $\mathbb{E}_\theta X^2 = \theta^2/2$, $\operatorname{Var}_\theta X = \theta^2/18$. (2) $\mathrm{MSE}(c) = c^2\mathbb{E} X^2 - 2c\theta\mathbb{E} X + \theta^2$; minimizing, $c = \theta\mathbb{E} X/\mathbb{E} X^2 = 4/3$, so $\delta(x) = 4x/3$. (3) $\mathbb{E}_\theta[4X/3] = 8\theta/9 \ne \theta$ — not unbiased. (4) $\mathbb{E}_\theta[\frac32 X - 2X^2] = \theta(1-\theta)$, so $\frac32 X - 2X^2$ is unbiased.
notes: MS comprehensive. Transcribed with solution from answer key.

prompt: Regression of kid's IQ on mom's IQ ($X_1$) and mom's age ($X_2$) with partial R output (some values blanked): $\hat\beta_0 = 17.596$, $\hat\beta_{X_1} = 0.604$ (SE 0.0587), $\hat\beta_{X_2} = 0.388$ (SE 0.326), residual se 18.26 on 431 df, $R^2 = 0.2036$; plus a nested anova(m2,m1) table. Answer: (1) sample size; (2) report fitted m1; (3) LS estimate of $\beta_1$ and interpretation; (4) test $\beta_1 = 0$ at 5%; (5) overall F statistic for m1; (6) t statistic for $\beta_2 = 0$; (7) $H_0, H_1$ of the anova(m2,m1) test; (8) the blanked A, B, F, df, p-value, and conclusion.
solution: (1) $n = 431 + 2 + 1 = 434$. (2) $\widehat{\text{kid\_score}} = 17.596 + 0.604\,\text{mom\_iq} + 0.388\,\text{mom\_age}$. (3) $\hat\beta_1 = 0.604$: each extra mom-IQ point raises predicted kid score by ~0.6, holding age fixed. (4) $T = 0.604/0.0587 = 10.28 > t_{431,.975}\approx1.97$ — reject. (5) With $\mathrm{RSS} = 143665$, $p = 2$, $R^2 = 0.2036 \Rightarrow \mathrm{TSS} = 180393$; $F = \frac{(\mathrm{TSS}-\mathrm{RSS})/2}{\mathrm{RSS}/431} \approx 55.1$. (6) $t = 0.388/0.326 = 1.19$. (7) $H_0: \beta_2 = 0$ vs $H_1: \beta_2 \ne 0$. (8) $A = 432 - 431 = 1$, $B = 144137 - 143665 = 472$; $F = \frac{B/A}{143665/431} \sim F_{1,431}$, p-value $0.2348$ — do not reject (mom_age not significant).
